newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ commodity prices still weak in May - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ commodity prices still weak in May - ANZ.

text.p: The average New Zealand dollar price of New Zealand's commodity exports showed a minor improvement in May, rising 0.1 percent after a 1.7 percent fall in April, ANZ Bank said on Wednesday.
ANZ said its commodity price index showed the corresponding average world price of New Zealand's commodity exports fell by 1.1 percent in May following a 2.5 percent drop in April.
The NZ dollar price index rose slightly to 98.2 from 98.1 in April and the world price index fell to 121.5 from 122.8 over the same period.
On an annual basis, the New Zealand dollar index fell 6.6 percent in May, while the world price index fell 4.8 percent.
ANZ Bank said the rise of the New Zealand dollar index, as world prices fell, was a result of the currency weakening, particularly against the yen but also against the U.S. dollar.

"New Zealand dollar commodity prices for fish, apples, lambs and skins weakened during May but this was offset to some degree by an improvement in prices for wool, aluminium, sawn timber and logs," it said.
ANZ said commodity prices were generally expected to strengthen over 1997/98 on the back of firmer world growth.
However, some markets continued to face high levels of production and stocks, which might delay or dampen further price improvements.
